# hypha

> hypha is a local-first, end-to-end encrypted notes app for macOS (Apple silicon), Windows, Linux, iPhone and iPad. Notes, a journal of your days and a small database of your life, synced peer-to-peer between your own devices. No account, no server, no one in between.

Site: https://hypha.miniml.net/ (English) and https://hypha.miniml.net/de/ (German).

## What it is

- Notes with a rich editor: headings, lists, tasks with due dates, tables, code, callouts, images, PDFs, whiteboards, links between notes, tags, notebooks and bookmarks (a colour that marks a note and a passage in it).
- Note types with properties (Recipe, Book, Movie, Person, Project, Task, Meeting, your own), and saved views of them as a table, a board or a calendar.
- A daily note for every day, with a stream of your days, and reminders.
- Search by words and by meaning (an on-device embedding model; nothing leaves the device), and a map of how notes connect.
- Sharing a vault with other people: every device holds the whole vault; a vault chat and comments on passages; roles are owner, member and relay.
- Import from Obsidian, any Markdown folder and Standard Notes backups; export as Markdown, PDF or a portable encrypted backup. Automatic backups by day, week and month.
- English and German interface.

## How sync works

- Every note is encrypted on the device before it travels, with keys derived from one passphrase. Keys live on your devices only.
- On the same Wi-Fi, devices find each other by themselves and sync directly.
- Across the internet, online at the same time, devices meet through a distributed hash table and connect end to end. The network that introduces them carries no notes.
- Devices that are never online together meet through an optional relay (hypha-peer): a small program you run on your own machine with Docker or systemd, or hypha's own relay while it is in beta (by invite code). A relay stores and forwards ciphertext and never holds a key.
- Edits made in two places merge without conflicts (CRDTs).

## Facts

- No account, no e-mail address, no telemetry, no analytics on the website.
- Cost: the apps are free. Licence: source-available (use, read, change and share at no charge; not for sale by others), not open source.
- Status: beta. The cryptography has not been audited yet. Intel Macs are not supported. iPhone and iPad come through TestFlight.
- Author: Marco Laux.
